title: QML-IDS Operating Points: reproducibility artifact for the Kaissar corpus
description:
Portable derived-data and software companion for False-Alarm Improvements and Detection Trade-Offs in QML Intrusion Detection: A Secondary Analysis of the Kaissar Corpus. The closed 25-entry frame yields 21 included articles (20 identified documentary families), with substantive methodological material consulted for 15. Five articles supply 24 main descriptive points; six points from two articles enter the principal conditional binomial illustration block; independence remains unverified.

The package preserves 466 derived records, source/version locations, deterministic calculations, independent numerical checks and figure/table generation. It distinguishes K17 descriptive comparisons, K10 separately identifiable FPR, K07 identification ranges, K03 observed rates versus hypothetical calculations and K11 training-described results. No primary document copies, manuscript PDFs, journal template, model training or QPU execution are included.

Licensing by scope: code under MIT; authors' derived data and documentation under CC BY 4.0. See LICENSE, LICENSE-DATA and LICENSING.txt. Neither licence overrides the rights in the original sources.

Version 2.2.0 applies a uniform provenance rule: K03 test-adjusted and K11 training-described rates remain descriptive, with hypothetical intervals only in the supplement. All 24 descriptive points and all source counts remain unchanged. K07 FPR rounding ranges are displayed. Historical ten-point calculations remain reproducible. Author validation is confirmed complete; no independent duplicate extraction is claimed.
